newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Lagging Nasdaq could signal tired market.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Lagging Nasdaq could signal tired market.

text.p: The Nasdaq composite index's failure to match other major indexes in record ground could be a signal U.S. stocks may be losing momentum, technical analysts said.
On Monday afternoon the Nasdaq composite index was up a fraction of a point at 1570, under its record high set July 16 1580.63.
Meanwhile the Dow industrials, the Standard & Poor's 500 and the New York Stock Exchange Composite index were trading in record ground, adding to new highs set on Thursday.
Ralph Bloch, chief technical analyst at Raymond, James and Associates, said a chart of NYSE net advancing issues was also under its record high levels.
As of Friday there had to be 667 more advancing issues than decliners for a record to be set, he said. On Monday afternoon there were 238 net advancers on the NYSE.

"These two indicators had better confirm really soon, in a matter of days," he said. "If the market should see some profit taking before these lagging indicators confirm, you could get a decline in the five to 10 percent range."
The Dow was up 62 points to 8175 on Monday afternoon, ahead of its record closing high of 8116.93.
Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities, said the lack of confirmation by Nasdaq was "a little bit worrisome" in the short term.
But he said other factors, including recent overall market breadth and the number of stocks making new highs, made it appear the market was not near a major top.
He said the ability of Microsoft Corp, a Nasdaq bellwether, to hold its July 21 intraday low of 133-3/4 could foreshadow action in the overall market.
If Microsoft were to break that support level, "that would tell you as much about the short-term direction of the market as anything else," Tower said.
Microsoft was off 1/2 at 138 on Monday afternoon.
Jonathan Dodd, technical analyst at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, said he saw near-term minor support for the Dow in the 7800-7850 level.

He said the market was charting a "steady as she goes" course, with up moves followed by brief periods of consolidation. He also said the market was benefiting from investors moving in and out of groups of stocks, broadening the rally.
"As long as we continue this group rotation we're getting and consolidate along the way, that's what you want to see," he said.
